en.marketHeading: What is actually different about marketing in {city}
market: Any campaign set to the Lower Mainland or to Metro Vancouver includes Vancouver, and Vancouver prices the auction. Set that targeting from an {city} business and you inherit the cost structure of a market whose customers are never going to drive an hour east to buy from you. The traffic looks fine in the report and the cost per acquisition quietly doubles. Meanwhile the reverse trip does happen, because plenty of Fraser Valley residents will go west, which is why the leak only ever runs in the direction that costs you money.

The second thing that makes {city} unusual is who the customer is. This is some of the most productive farmland in the country and a major road-freight corridor to the United States border, so a large share of businesses here sell to buyers who are nowhere near the Fraser Valley. If you are in {industries}, your market may be national or cross-border, and a local radius is not a conservative choice, it is the wrong shape entirely.

Underneath both of those, local demand is real and growing at 8.4%, comfortably above the national rate. There is a genuine {city} and Mission market for anything people buy close to home, and it is far cheaper to win than the equivalent search in Surrey or Vancouver. The plan just has to be explicit about which of the two businesses you are, because the answer changes almost every setting.

faq.q: Do you have an office in {city}?
faq.a: No. I am based in Toronto and work from home, so there is no {city} office and I am not going to imply there is. Everything is run remotely over video and email, which is how I run every account. If you want someone who will walk into your shop, I am the wrong hire and I will say so on the call rather than after you have paid.

faq.q: Should we include Vancouver in our targeting?
faq.a: Only if Vancouver customers realistically buy from you, and for most {city} businesses they do not. Including the city means paying its auction prices across your whole campaign to reach people who have a dozen closer options. Taking it out is usually the single biggest cost improvement available on a Fraser Valley account.

faq.q: Most of our customers are not local. Does local marketing help us?
faq.a: Local search will not, and I would rather say that than sell it to you. If you sell into national or cross-border supply chains, what works is being findable and credible on the specifics of what you make or move, which is SEO and AI visibility work aimed at the buyer rather than the neighbourhood.

faq.q: Is {city} cheaper to advertise in than Surrey or Vancouver?
faq.a: Generally yes, sometimes substantially, which is exactly why the accidental Vancouver overlap is so costly. I will not put a number on the gap until I have pulled the real figures for your category, because a made-up benchmark is worse than none.
Google Ads management is $1,500 a month plus your ad spend. SEO consulting is $1,200 a month. AIO consulting is $1,800 one time. No setup fees and no long contract.
